title: Between record debt and high school protests, France's situation draws global attention
subhead: The mobilization of French high school students has sparked major media coverage and political reactions in the United States, Italy, Belgium and the United Kingdom. Only a few countries, such as Germany – preoccupied with its own domestic political debates – have treated the issue with restraint.

New York mayor will ask Trump to withdraw ICE after shooting
subhead: On Thursday afternoon, federal immigration agents shot a man in his car while a 5-year-old was present. Mayor Zohran Mamdani said that he plans on calling Trump and demanding an end to all ICE operations in New York City. ICE has been involved in several high-profile shootings this year, including the killing of two US citizens in Minneapolis.

title: Paris officials seek to reduce the area under heritage protection in the capital
subhead: The left-wing municipal majority plans to review the perimeters of what is considered a 'Remarkable Heritage Site,' which it deems too extensive. Currently, the site includes the first seven arrondissements of the capital, as well as parts of four others.

title: Lutetia wall: 'An archeological discovery can be instantaneous, but knowledge never is'
subhead: Following the discovery of a Gallic wall at the Hôtel-Dieu hospital in Paris, archeologist William Van Andringa writes for Le Monde that we cannot make stones speak before we have truly questioned them.

title: The letter of imprisoned Russian journalist Ivan Safronov: 'Like Jean Valjean, I know what captivity is, and I know how to cherish freedom'
subhead: Safronov, a prisoner of conscience who was arrested in 2020 and is now detained in Siberia, turns to literature as a lifeline. He recently reread Victor Hugo's Les Misérables. Here is the letter he sent to Le Monde about this classic.

title: Canadian writer Anne Carson awarded 2026 Nobel Prize in literature
subhead: The Canadian writer received the Swedish Academy's highest honor on Thursday, October 8. A master of textual deviation, Carson, who began as a classical philologist, blends poetry and popular culture, prose and verse, with both humor and erudition.

title: Heatwaves killed over 8,000 people in France this year. Here are some of their stories
subhead: The French health authorities reported that 8,124 deaths were related to the extreme heatwaves between late May and late August in France. Le Monde spoke to the friends and families of 11 of the victims to find out about the lives behind those numbers.
